first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 shows activation messaging improved week-one engagement and drove first meaningful actions. Memory_86 demonstrates that shortening onboarding improves completion rates. These two levers together address both the activation decline and onboarding completion drop. I'm verifying memory_86 (onboarding improvements) and memory_73 (promotional pricing risks) to confirm: (1) whether the onboarding lift from memory_86 was durable and what drove it, since completion is now declining; and (2) to ensure we avoid the retention damage that promotional pricing caused (memory_73), which would harm long-term qualified revenue despite addressing near-term SMB churn. Activation messaging carries no known retention risk (memory_91), directly targets the current activation decline, and avoids the generalization hazard of promotional pricing. A standard experiment on activation messaging preserves uncertainty about scale while addressing the immediate problem.
